question: Under each dataset's frozen length contract, which effective knobs merit later dev search, and which route or candidate mechanisms are inactive or harmful?

base.features: TF-ISF v2, stopwords on, sublinear TF on, unigrams, importance weight 1.0 and all other base-feature weights 0

correctness_precondition.change: Add features.position.scope=document and compute the position prior from canonical document_position, resetting at each document boundary.
correctness_precondition.reason: The current feature receives only the flattened sentence list; enabling it on Multi-News would encode cross-document concatenation order rather than within-document position.
correctness_precondition.success: Golden multi-document test proves both document starts receive 1.0; missing sentence records fail loudly when document scope is requested.

fixed_not_searched: data policy, partition manifest, evaluator and all-row denominator
semantic batch size, device and max_model_tokens after a truncation/cost preflight
sparse graph implementation, convergence tolerance and iteration ceiling
output ordering, require_nonempty and word-count unit
excluded_as_invalid_or_redundant: TF-ISF v1 because it has a documented length/repetition defect
dense graph base feature because GovReport requires bounded sparse graph
length feature until its documented formula mismatch is resolved
centrality and novelty base weights because they are degenerate and duplicate route semantics
coverage_method=set because the canonical evaluator treats it as the same facility-location definition as max
coverage_method=diversity because it double-counts redundancy and is rejected by the objective factory
group_coverage because it is not implemented and fails loudly
adaptive compute mode because it is not implemented

measurement.primary_screen_score: all-row mean of per-document macro mean(ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-Lsum)

promotion_rule: Use dev deltas only to rank follow-up effort. Promote a knob when it improves the primary screen score without an upper-bound/schema/denominator failure and either has the same sign on both primary datasets or has a predeclared task-profile explanation for a dataset-specific effect. Do not observe dev-test during this screening.
route_deletion_rule: A route is not deleted from a cheap ROUGE screen alone. After the screen, run candidate recall and unique-contribution diagnostics on dev. Apply ARCHITECTURE sections 5.3 and 5.4: delete semantic without unique validated candidate recall or quality gain; delete graph when it has no incremental effect beyond semantic or is highly redundant.
